options.C: Report the Project as defective, as a configured Project should follow whatever it has been given
options.D: Leave the configuration alone and correct each mis-triaged work order by hand as it appears

rationale.correct: Instructions govern behavior, knowledge supplies facts, Skills define procedures, scoped Memory holds continuity. A vendor directory is facts and belongs in knowledge; a step-by-step procedure is a Skill's job. A need placed in the wrong mechanism produces exactly this: a configuration that looks complete and does not hold.

distractors.B: Loading everything into instructions swells one mechanism to do three jobs; the mismatch that causes the wandering remains.
distractors.C: Nothing is defective: each mechanism is doing its own job on material that belongs to a different one.
distractors.D: Hand-correcting work orders treats the output symptom while the misplaced configuration keeps generating it.

questions.question: A match operations coordinator at a sports league uses a file-storage connector so Claude can read fixture documents. A request to have Claude reorganize the storage folders themselves and change their sharing permissions keeps failing, and the coordinator has rewritten the prompt four times. What is the most appropriate reading of the failures?

options.A: The prompt still is not worded clearly enough, and a fifth, more precise rewrite is the next step
options.B: The request sits beyond the connector's capability edge — a scope problem no prompt wording will fix
options.C: More connectors should be installed until one of them manages the reorganization
options.D: Connectors let Claude do whatever the connected app can do, so the storage service must be down

rationale.correct: Every connector extends reach up to a capability edge, and a request that fails at the boundary is a scope problem, not a prompt problem. Knowing the connector's edge is what prevents misrouted fixes — four rewrites have already shown that wording is not the variable.

distractors.A: A fifth rewrite iterates on the component that four failures have already cleared; the boundary does not move for phrasing.
distractors.C: Stacking connectors adds machinery in the hope one exceeds its design; the task belongs in the storage service's own admin tools.
distractors.D: A connector exposes a defined slice of an app's capability, not all of it; inferring an outage from a scope limit invents a mechanism.

questions.question: A member services manager at a wine distribution cooperative is about to load a shared folder — supplier price lists, tasting notes going back years, assorted policy PDFs, none with a clear owner — into a Project's knowledge for answering member questions. Which TWO controls should be applied before the folder becomes Project knowledge? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Upload the entire folder unfiltered so retrieval has the most possible material to draw on
options.B: Trust the files as they stand, since everything in the folder came from inside the cooperative
options.C: Add a standing notice to outputs warning members that the underlying knowledge may be outdated
options.D: Screen each file for authority and currency, and record an owner for what stays
options.E: Scope the upload to what member questions actually need, with a review cadence for keeping it current

rationale.correct: Uploaded knowledge needs provenance — authority, currency, scope, and a review cadence — or stale and unowned content is treated as authoritative. Retrieval scope is a quality control, not a recall maximizer: screening for authority and currency with a named owner, and scoping the upload with a review cadence, are the two controls that give the knowledge a warrant.

distractors.A: Maximum material is maximum unvetted authority; years-old tasting notes answer member questions with the same standing as current price lists.
distractors.B: Internal origin is not authority or currency; the folder's problem is age and ownerlessness, which residing inside the cooperative does not cure.
distractors.C: A staleness notice discloses the defect to members instead of fixing it; the knowledge underneath stays unowned and unscreened.

questions.question: A program specialist at an airline loyalty program office maintains a Project whose knowledge holds last year's policy manual and a newer benefits bulletin, and the two disagree on upgrade-voucher rules. Depending on which document retrieval surfaces, member replies cite different rules. What is the most appropriate resolution?

options.A: Leave both documents in place, as the model reliably prefers the newer document when sources disagree
options.B: Remove the older manual from knowledge entirely so no conflict can ever arise
options.C: Have Claude merge the two documents into one combined summary and answer from that
options.D: Record which document governs which scope, apply that precedence, and state the resolution in replies

rationale.correct: When two knowledge authorities conflict, the resolution is by documented scope and precedence, stated in the output — never silently averaged or decided by which source is newer. The manual and the bulletin each govern something; writing down which governs the voucher rules is the fix that holds.

distractors.A: No mechanism guarantees the newer source wins retrieval; the claim invents a preference and leaves replies to chance.
distractors.B: Deleting the manual removes everything else it still governs; the conflict needed a precedence decision, not an amputation.
distractors.C: A blended summary launders the disagreement into unattributed prose; members get a rule neither document actually states.

questions.question: A funding coordinator at an apprenticeship training provider re-uploaded the Project's entire folder of funding-rule PDFs last week, so every file shows a fresh date. A teammate points to those dates as proof the Project's knowledge is current. The coordinator knows one agency revised its rules two months ago. What is the most appropriate response?

options.A: Agree with the teammate: files uploaded last week are current by any reasonable standard
options.B: Re-upload the folder monthly from now on so the file dates never age more than a few weeks
options.C: Check the content against the agency's current rules — a fresh upload timestamp is not provenance
options.D: Keep the files as they are and add a caveat to outputs that funding rules may have changed

rationale.correct: File-level metadata is not content provenance: a fresh upload timestamp says nothing about whether the content is current, and treating one as the other is how stale knowledge acquires authority. The agency revised its rules two months ago; only checking the content against the current rules answers the currency question.

distractors.A: The date records when the file moved, not when the rules did; the two-month-old revision is invisible to the timestamp.
distractors.B: A monthly re-upload refreshes the metadata on the same stale content; shrinking the interval never touches the actual rules.
distractors.D: A caveat discloses the risk to readers instead of resolving it; the outdated rule keeps flowing into funded decisions.

questions.question: A bid manager at an architecture firm added a standing instruction to the team's Project months ago: "keep our bid responses compelling and on-brand." Bid drafts look the same as before the instruction existed; nothing has errored and nothing has visibly changed. What is the most appropriate fix?

options.A: Rewrite the instruction into precise, testable rules whose effect on a draft can be observed
options.B: Strengthen the wording — "always make every response truly compelling" — so the model takes it seriously
options.C: Ask Claude whether it has been following the instruction, and close the matter if it says yes
options.D: Leave it for now and put a full instructions overhaul on next quarter's improvement list

rationale.correct: Standing instructions must be precise and testable: a vague instruction fails silently — nothing errors and nothing changes, exactly what the bid drafts show. Each rule is written so its effect on an output can be observed, which is what makes the instruction verifiable rather than decorative.

distractors.B: Adding intensity to vagueness is still vagueness; no observable behavior is specified, so silence continues.
distractors.C: A self-report is not an observation; the instruction's problem is that compliance and non-compliance look identical.
distractors.D: Deferral leaves a silent failure in place for a quarter; the fix is one rewritten instruction, not a program.

questions.question: A membership officer at an art museum notices two habits in the team's renewal-letter Project. The office's durable drafting rules are restated by hand in every request, and drafts have recently begun calling one donor "the museum's premier partner" — phrasing that turns out to come from a line inside a sponsor-supplied PDF in the Project's knowledge. What is the most appropriate correction?

options.A: Print the drafting rules on a cover page added to each uploaded document so the rules travel with the files
options.B: Keep both habits and strip the premier-partner phrasing out of each draft after generation
options.C: Restate the drafting rules more emphatically in each request so they outweigh anything in the files
options.D: Put the durable rules into the Project's instructions, and treat uploaded content as data with no instruction authority

rationale.correct: A rule that must always hold lives in trusted, durable configuration — never restated per request and never inside the material it governs. Content in knowledge sources is data: the sponsor PDF's self-serving line acquired the authority of an instruction, which is precisely what the separation exists to prevent.

distractors.A: A cover page puts the rules inside the governed material itself — the layer whose contents must never carry instruction authority.
distractors.B: Post-editing removes the phrase draft by draft while the PDF keeps issuing it; the authority confusion is untouched.
distractors.C: Emphatic per-request restatement is the fragile habit the fix should retire; volume does not make the placement right.

questions.question: A customer success lead at a b2b software company configured a Project a year ago: product names in the instructions, packaging documents in knowledge, and a report-formatting Skill. The product line has since been renamed and repackaged. Account summaries have grown subtly off-target, and at no point did anything error or warn. What is the most appropriate lesson to draw?

options.A: Configurations surface their own problems eventually, and customer complaints will say when to act
options.B: Configurations age against a changing world, so reviews must be scheduled — the decay sends no signal
options.C: The Project should be rebuilt from scratch every month so no element can ever age
options.D: Configured Projects are unreliable, and the team should paste fresh context into every session instead

rationale.correct: Instructions, knowledge, Skills versions, and Memory all age against a changing world, and because the quality decay produces no warning signal, maintenance runs on scheduled reviews rather than on triggers. A year of renames and repackaging drifting silently into summaries is the signature of unscheduled configuration.

distractors.A: Complaints are the decay finally reaching customers; a lagging alarm made of other people's frustration is not a maintenance plan.
distractors.C: A monthly rebuild scraps working configuration wholesale; the discipline is a scheduled review of what changed, not perpetual reconstruction.
distractors.D: Abandoning configuration trades silent aging for loud, daily re-keying; the leverage was real, it just needed maintenance.

questions.question: An events coordinator at a botanical garden tightens the shared Project's instructions, changing how event budget summaries are structured. Three other teams pull those summaries into their own reporting. The new configuration is live and producing better output. What else does the change require?

options.A: Nothing — the summaries improved, and drawing attention to the change would invite needless debate
options.B: A line in the Project description noting that configurations may change at any time
options.C: Telling the three teams what changed in the summaries their reporting depends on
options.D: Holding the news for the annual configuration review, where all changes are presented together

rationale.correct: A configuration change that alters shared outputs is announced to the people who depend on them — to inform dependents is part of the maintenance obligation, not a courtesy. Three teams' reporting consumes these summaries; their pipelines meet the new structure either by notice or by surprise.

distractors.A: Better output does not excuse a silent interface change; the downstream teams absorb the breakage without knowing why.
distractors.B: A may-change disclaimer discloses the possibility of change while communicating nothing about this change.
distractors.D: An annual digest informs the dependents months after their reporting already hit the new structure.

questions.question: A resourcing coordinator at a recruitment process outsourcing provider wants Claude to summarize interview notes into a shortlist brief for the client's hiring manager. The provider's AI policy permits candidate-related work but requires every use case to be screened first, and the team has been treating that screen as a yes-or-no gate. How should the coordinator screen this use case?

options.A: Rule it inappropriate, as any work touching candidate material is off limits to AI
options.B: Ask Claude to weigh the use case against the provider's policy and adopt the verdict it returns
options.C: Approve it outright, as the briefs stay inside the account team and no candidate reads one
options.D: Score it on reversibility, consequence, human element and accountability, and land it as appropriate-with-review

rationale.correct: The four screening criteria — reversibility, consequence, human element and accountability — classify a use case as appropriate, appropriate-with-review, or inappropriate, and the middle verdict is the common one. A shortlist brief is reversible before it reaches the hiring manager, carries real consequence for candidates, and has a human element throughout, which places it in the middle band with a named reviewer instead of at either pole.

distractors.A: A blanket exclusion answers the screen before it is run; the criteria exist to separate candidate work that needs a reviewer from work that cannot be delegated at all.
distractors.B: The model's reading of a policy is not a screening verdict, and accountability for the classification stays with the coordinator who runs it.
distractors.C: Internal circulation is not one of the four criteria; the consequence the shortlist brief carries for a candidate is unchanged by who reads the document.

questions.question: A sales coordinator at a craft brewery sales cooperative is drafting the members' bulletin with Claude. The cooperative's AI policy is a single page: it permits AI drafting for member communications and asks the practitioner to stay within it. The draft repeats a supplier's unverified claim about a competitor's hop contracts, a situation the policy does not address. What should the coordinator do?

options.A: Send it as drafted, as the policy permits AI drafting for member communications
options.B: Decide this one against the boundaries the policy sets, and record the reasoning for the call
options.C: Pass every bulletin the policy does not explicitly cover to the compliance lead
options.D: Add a footer saying the bulletin was drafted with AI assistance, and send it

rationale.correct: Governance standards bound the call; they do not make it. Responsible use is exercised by the practitioner one decision at a time, so the unverified claim about a competitor is the coordinator's to resolve, and the policy's silence on it is not permission.

distractors.A: Permission to draft with AI is not permission to publish an unverified claim; the policy bounds the work and leaves this judgment in the practitioner’s hands.
distractors.C: Routing every uncovered case upward turns a practitioner skill into a queue, and the bulletin waits while a one-page policy is asked to do work it was never written to do.
distractors.D: Naming the drafting tool tells members how the text was produced and nothing about whether the claim it repeats is true.

questions.question: An operations analyst at a dental clinic network wants to load a year of appointment records — patient names, treatment codes, contact details — into a Project so Claude can analyze no-show patterns. The upload window is short and the analysis is due to the network board this week. Which TWO steps belong before the records enter the Project? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Upload the export now and pull anything sensitive back out if a concern is raised later
options.B: Ask Claude to confirm that the export is safe to upload, then proceed on that confirmation
options.C: Classify the export against the network's data policy before any of it moves
options.D: Match the handling to that classification: strip patient identifiers and scope the Project
options.E: Write into the Project instructions that the records are confidential and must not be shared

rationale.correct: Data sensitivity is established before data enters a feature: classify first, then match the handling. Appointment records carry patient identifiers, so the privacy considerations are settled by classifying the export and by stripping identifiers and scoping the Project — the check happens before the records move, not after an incident.

distractors.A: Pulling data back out after it has landed is incident response, not a control; the identifiers are already inside the Project when the concern arrives.
distractors.B: The model has no view of the network's data policy or of what the export contains, so its reassurance is fluent, not a classification.
distractors.E: A confidentiality instruction governs how Claude behaves once the records are in the Project, and says nothing about whether they should have entered it.

questions.question: A claims analyst on an insurance claims intake team needs a summary of a disputed claim file that contains policyholder national identification numbers and medical notes. Under the team's handling rules, regulated identifiers must not leave the team's own systems for any outside service, though the claim narrative itself carries no such restriction. The adjuster has asked for the summary within the hour. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Remove or anonymize the regulated identifiers, then run the summary on the redacted file
options.B: Do this summary by hand, as regulated claim files cannot involve an external tool at all
options.C: Instruct the model not to retain or reuse the identifiers, then upload the file unchanged
options.D: Upload the file unchanged and mark the summary confidential before it reaches the adjuster

rationale.correct: Redaction before entry is the control that lets restricted work proceed: with the regulated identifiers removed or anonymized, the claim narrative can be summarized without breaching the regulatory restriction, and privacy is protected by what never entered the tool. Abandoning the task was not required.

distractors.B: The policy restricts the regulated data, not the work; a redacted file still carries the claim narrative the adjuster needs.
distractors.C: An instruction to the model is a request about behavior, not a control over data that has already left the team’s hands.
distractors.D: A confidentiality marking describes how the summary should be treated, after the identifiers were already sent.

questions.question: A research associate at an executive search firm discusses candidate dossiers with Claude across several surfaces during one search: a shared team workspace with Memory switched on, a connector into the firm’s document store, and a personal chat. The dossiers include compensation histories and references given in confidence. Which consideration should decide where this work happens?

options.A: Whether the surfaces sit under the firm's single enterprise agreement, which makes them equivalent
options.B: Whether Memory can be cleared at the end of the search, once the dossiers have been discussed
options.C: Whether pasting short excerpts instead of whole dossiers keeps the volume of data low
options.D: Where the dossier content comes to rest on each surface — retention, Memory, connector scope

rationale.correct: Different entry points carry different retention and handling properties, so the destination is part of the data sensitivity decision: a private session, Memory controls, and the scope of a connector each change where confidential references end up. The surface is chosen before the dossier is discussed, not audited afterward.

distractors.A: One commercial agreement does not make retention, Memory and connector scope identical across surfaces; the handling properties differ per entry point.
distractors.B: Clearing Memory at the end treats a retention decision as cleanup, and the confidential references were retained for the weeks in between.
distractors.C: Excerpting lowers the volume while leaving the sensitive content on the same surface with the same retention properties.

questions.question: A member services team at a credit union routes support drafting through Claude and keeps every prompt and response in a debugging log held indefinitely. The logs contain member account numbers and dispute details, and the team values them because a full history makes tracing a bad draft quick. What should change?

options.A: Nothing, as a full history is what makes tracing a bad draft quick and the log stays internal
options.B: Switch the logging off, so no member data can be retained anywhere in the workflow
options.C: Keep identifiers out of what is logged, and hold the rest only as long as policy allows
options.D: Leave the logs as they are and restrict access to the two support supervisors

rationale.correct: Retention and logging scope are governed decisions: sensitive content is kept only as policy allows, and debugging convenience is not a basis for holding account numbers forever. Stripping identifiers at the point of logging leaves the team the trace it relies on and settles the privacy considerations in the same change.

distractors.A: Internal storage still stores; an indefinite log of member account numbers widens the exposure every day it is kept.
distractors.B: Removing the log removes the traceability the team depends on, when the question was what the log holds and for how long.
distractors.D: Narrowing who can read the log leaves the account numbers retained indefinitely, which is the decision under question.

questions.question: A procurement officer at a mining site office is asked by the site manager to run supplier tender documents through Claude for comparison. Organizational policy blocks tender material from external tools until a review is signed off. The site manager argues that the risk the policy targets does not arise at this remote site, and that the tender closes on Monday. What is the most appropriate response?

options.A: Run the comparison for this tender, as the policy's risk does not arise at this site
options.B: Take an exception request to the named policy owner, with the process and compensating controls
options.C: Ask Claude whether the intended use falls inside the policy, and act on its reading
options.D: Park the comparison until the policy comes up at its next scheduled review

rationale.correct: Organizational AI policies bind even where a use looks locally harmless, and the exception path runs through a named human authority with a documented process and compensating controls. A closing date is a reason to raise the exception quickly, not a reason for the practitioner to grant one.

distractors.A: A local reading of the risk substitutes the practitioner’s judgment for the control; the policy binds until a named authority says otherwise.
distractors.C: A model’s reading of a policy carries no authority to permit an exception to it.
distractors.D: Waiting for the next review lets the tender close with no answer, when the exception process exists to be used at speed.

questions.question: A documentation officer at an engineering standards secretariat finds a community-published Skill that formats draft standards into the house layout. It carries thousands of installs and strong ratings, and it would save the team hours every week. What should happen before it is enabled?

options.A: Enable it, as thousands of installs and strong ratings are the evidence that matters here
options.B: Enable it and watch the first few formatted drafts for anything unexpected
options.C: Ban community Skills at the secretariat and build the formatter in-house
options.D: Evaluate the Skill's source and the permissions it requests, as with any installed software

rationale.correct: A Skill is software: its source and permissions are evaluated before enabling it, because extending capability is a supply-chain decision and not a convenience toggle. Popularity describes how many other teams took the same risk, not what the Skill can reach once it runs inside the secretariat’s Project.

distractors.A: Install counts and ratings measure popularity, not what permissions the Skill requests or where its code comes from.
distractors.B: Watching the output catches formatting mistakes; it does not reveal what the Skill reached while producing them.
distractors.C: A blanket ban gives up a real capability to avoid a review that takes an afternoon.

questions.question: A curriculum lead at an industrial safety training company learns that a newer model tier has been released. The team’s Projects generate course assessments from regulator-approved material. Half the group wants everything moved across today; the other half wants the current tier frozen for the year. What is the most appropriate course of action?

options.A: Compare the new tier against the current baseline on the same assessments, then stage the rollout
options.B: Move every Project to the new tier now, as a newer release supersedes the one it replaces
options.C: Freeze the current tier for the year, so nothing that works today can change
options.D: Adopt the new tier and refresh the Project instructions and prompts in the same pass

rationale.correct: A vendor model change enters the organization's change-control path like any release: a like-for-like comparison against a baseline, a staged rollout, and a rollback path. Regulator-approved material raises the cost of an unmeasured switch, and it does not turn an indefinite freeze into a governance position.

distractors.B: Being newer is a release fact, not a fitness result for these assessments; the comparison is what makes the tier’s behavior known.
distractors.C: A permanent freeze avoids the comparison instead of running it, and the current tier ages against the material it is asked to assess.
distractors.D: Changing the tier and the instructions together leaves no way to attribute any difference in the assessments to either one.

questions.question: An admissions officer at a language school is asked by a partner agent to have Claude draft visa-supporting statements for applicants from their immigration paperwork. Policy blocks immigration documents from the tool, the agent is a major referral source, and enrollment closes this week. What is the most appropriate way to handle the request?

options.A: Split the paperwork into extracts small enough that no single request meets the blocked description
options.B: Do it quietly this once for the referral relationship, and raise the policy question later
options.C: Name the boundary to the agent, offer the permitted alternative, and log the escalation
options.D: Reply that the request is not permitted and close the conversation there

rationale.correct: Refusing well is part of responsible use: name the boundary, offer the permitted alternative — a statement drafted from the applicant's own school records — and follow the escalation and logging policy. A referral relationship and a closing date shape how quickly the alternative is offered, not whether the control holds.

distractors.A: Decomposing the request keeps the immigration content flowing while defeating the control that was written to stop it.
distractors.B: Quiet compliance leaves the school exposed and the policy untested, and the pressure is the condition the control exists for.
distractors.D: A flat refusal holds the line and abandons the agent, when a permitted route to a supporting statement exists.

questions.question: A volunteer coordinator at a hospice service wants Claude to summarize volunteers' visit notes into a weekly care-team digest. The notes describe families' circumstances in ordinary, unremarkable language, and nobody on the team can say whether this crosses a line. The coordinator's instinct is that it feels wrong. How should the case be settled?

options.A: Follow the instinct, as a use that feels uncomfortable to the coordinator is one to leave alone
options.B: Reason it through against the four screening criteria and record the verdict and its grounds
options.C: Treat it as settled by another region's approval of the same volunteer-note summaries
options.D: Send it to the ethics committee, which is what ambiguous cases are escalated for

rationale.correct: Ethical risk hides in ordinary outputs, and ambiguous cases are reasoned through against the stated screening criteria instead of resolved by instinct: the same reversibility, consequence, human element and accountability questions decide the hard case, and the recorded reasoning is what makes the verdict defensible to the care team.

distractors.A: Discomfort is a prompt to run the screen, not a verdict, and an unrecorded instinct cannot be reviewed or applied to the next case.
distractors.C: Another region's approval was a verdict on its own facts; what transfers between cases is the criteria, not the conclusion.
distractors.D: Escalating skips a screen the coordinator can run today, and the digest waits on a committee for a call the criteria already answer.

questions.question: A registrar's office at a community college uses Claude to draft the outcome paragraph in financial-aid appeal letters. A staff member reads and signs every letter before it goes out, and students receive the letter as the decision on their appeal. What does this workflow still owe the student?

options.A: Nothing further, as naming the drafting tool would invite challenges to sound decisions
options.B: Nothing further, as the staff member's signature is the accountability the student needs
options.C: A disclosure line added once a student asks whether the letter was AI-drafted
options.D: Disclosure of the AI involvement and a named route to contest the outcome

rationale.correct: Where an output affects a person's decision, disclosure of AI involvement and a route to contest the outcome belong in the design of the workflow. They are due-process obligations owed to the student, and fairness is what they protect — they are not courtesies added once someone complains.

distractors.A: Withholding how the letter was produced protects the office from questions, at the cost of the student’s ability to ask them.
distractors.B: A signature records who is accountable; it does not tell the student how the decision was produced or how to challenge it.
distractors.C: A disclosure that appears only when a student thinks to ask is not part of the design, and most students will never know to ask.

questions.question: A scheduling clerk at a ferry and harbor operations office asks Claude each morning for a plain-language summary of the day's sailing changes. For two weeks the summaries have been leaving out berth reassignments, and the team's view is that the tool has simply stopped being good at this. What should the clerk do first?

options.A: Move the summaries to the top model tier, as the current tier is evidently not capable enough
options.B: Open a vendor ticket reporting that the model has become unreliable for sailing summaries
options.C: Work the diagnostic sequence in order — specification, context, feature, configuration
options.D: Rewrite the prompt, reload the berth reference table, and switch the Project Skill in one pass

rationale.correct: Underperformance has discoverable causes, checked in a fixed order: the diagnostic sequence runs specification, context, feature, configuration, cheapest and most likely first. Summaries that drop berth reassignments most often trace to a specification that never named them or a context that no longer carries them, and both are found before the tool is blamed.

distractors.A: A larger tier answers a capability question nobody has established, when the omission may be a field the prompt never asked for.
distractors.B: Reporting a fault hands the diagnosis away before the four cheap checks inside the team’s own reach have been run.
distractors.D: Three changes at once removes any way of knowing which layer was at fault, and leaves the same uncertainty next time.

questions.question: A studio coordinator at a packaging design studio has the evidence in hand: the artwork-spec summaries Claude produces omit the print finish and the die-line reference on every job, including jobs whose brief stated both. Several fixes are on the table and each has a supporter. What determines which fix is the right one?

options.A: Naming the layer that failed — the prompt, the context, the feature choice or the configuration
options.B: Connecting the studio's job-tracking system so that Claude can pull each job's details for itself
options.C: Adding the print finish and die-line reference to each summary by hand as jobs come through
options.D: Applying the fix that worked on the client-brief prompts last month, which felt much the same

rationale.correct: Isolate before you fix: to diagnose here is to name whether the failure is the prompt, the context, the feature choice or the configuration, since each layer implies a different remedy. Briefs that stated both fields and summaries that drop both point at the specification, and a fix applied without a named cause is a guess, however well it worked elsewhere.

distractors.B: The briefs already carry both fields, so access to the job details is not what is missing; extending reach through a connector places the remedy at a layer no evidence points to.
distractors.C: Filling the gaps by hand keeps the summaries usable and leaves whatever drops the fields exactly as it is.
distractors.D: A fix that worked on a different failure is a borrowed conclusion; the layer at fault here has still not been named.

questions.question: A development officer at an orchestra development office has spent three weeks refining a prompt that drafts major-donor renewal letters. The drafts come back strong, accurate and warm, and every one still needs a fundraiser's edit before it can be sent. The office had promised the board a workflow that produces mail-ready letters. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: The prompt needs further refinement, until the drafts come back ready to mail unchanged
options.B: The workflow needs a higher model tier, as a stronger model would close the remaining gap
options.C: Claude should rate its own drafts, and the ones it scores as mail-ready can go out unedited
options.D: The expectation is the mismatch: what was promised was a finished letter, not a strong draft

rationale.correct: Expectation mismatch is a legitimate diagnosis: sometimes nothing is broken except what was promised. Drafts that are strong, accurate and warm and still need a fundraiser's edit describe a working assistive workflow, and the honest remedy is to reset the promise made to the board instead of tuning what already delivers.

distractors.A: Three weeks of refinement have produced strong drafts; more of the same tuning chases a target that was set wrong.
distractors.B: A stronger model produces a better draft, and a better draft is still a draft that a fundraiser signs off.
distractors.C: A self-assessment reports how confident the model is, not whether the letter is ready for a major donor.

questions.question: An audit coordinator at a food safety auditing firm improved the firm's report drafts in one afternoon: the prompt was rewritten, a knowledge file of past audit reports was added, and the Project was moved to a higher model tier. The drafts are visibly better, and the partners want to know what worked so it can be applied to the other report types. What should the coordinator do?

options.A: Report that the combination works, as the three changes together produced the better drafts
options.B: Rebuild the baseline and reintroduce the three changes one at a time to see which carries the gain
options.C: Credit the tier move, as a model change is the largest of the three levers pulled that afternoon
options.D: Ask Claude which of the three changes improved its drafts, and pass that answer to the partners

rationale.correct: Attribution requires a reconstructed baseline and one changed variable at a time. Three changes in one afternoon read as decisiveness and leave the firm unable to say what to carry across to the other report types: the gain is real and unattributed, which is the same as untransferable.

distractors.A: A combination that works is not a finding that transfers; the other report types would inherit changes that may contribute nothing.
distractors.C: The size of a lever is a prior, not a measurement, and the prompt rewrite is at least as plausible a cause.
distractors.D: The model holds no record of the prompt it ran under yesterday and no view of the tier move, so the answer would be a plausible guess.

questions.question: A paralegal at a support bureau asks Claude to summarize a document bundle for a client matter, and the request is declined. The same kind of summary ran without trouble last quarter, the bundle now includes another firm's privileged correspondence, and the filing deadline is Thursday. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Rephrase the request in smaller pieces until the refusal stops appearing
options.B: Report it as a product fault and wait for the vendor to restore the earlier behavior
options.C: Check the request against the task, current policy and permissions, then redo the permitted part
options.D: Switch off the bureau’s policy configuration for the session so the summary can be produced

rationale.correct: A refusal is diagnosed against the task, current policy and permissions, and any recent change: a bundle that now carries another firm's privileged correspondence is a different task from last quarter's. The permitted portion is then redesigned and done, or the work is escalated — evading or stripping the control is never the fix.

distractors.A: Reshaping the request until it passes treats the control as an obstacle, and the privileged correspondence is still in the bundle.
distractors.B: Waiting on the vendor assumes a defect, when what changed is the bundle, and the deadline does not move.
distractors.D: Turning the configuration off removes the control that caught the problem and leaves the privileged material untouched.

questions.question: A trading assistant at a specialty coffee importer sends the weekly market update to the desk head, who replies that it is too generic to be useful and nothing more. The assistant plans to be more careful with the next one. What should happen instead?

options.A: Turn the critique into one named change: state the buyer segment and the origins to cover
options.B: Add a line to the prompt asking for higher quality and more specific market writing
options.C: Rewrite the prompt, attach a file of past updates, and lengthen the output in one revision
options.D: Circulate the next update to the whole desk and act on whatever comments come back

rationale.correct: A disappointing output is data: the critique is translated into one specific adjustment aimed at the component it names, not into a general resolve to do better. Too generic points at an unspecified audience and scope, so the feedback becomes a stated buyer segment and a stated set of origins — a change whose effect on the next update can be seen.

distractors.B: Asking for higher quality restates the complaint inside the prompt and names nothing the next draft can act on.
distractors.C: Three simultaneous changes make the next update better or worse with no way to say which of them did it.
distractors.D: Another round of desk opinions gathers more critique, when the one already given has not been converted into a change.

questions.question: A scheduler at a landscaping services franchise finds a phrasing that makes Claude include crew size and equipment in every route-plan summary, which the earlier phrasing kept dropping. It works reliably. Six other schedulers across the franchise hit the same problem every week. What should be done with the fix?

options.A: Post the working phrasing in the team chat, where any scheduler can search for it later
options.B: Leave it as know-how, since the schedulers who need it will work the phrasing out as they go
options.C: Rebuild the route-planning Project from scratch around the new phrasing
options.D: Write it into the Project instructions or a Skill, so every scheduler gets it by default

rationale.correct: A fix that worked is captured so it persists beyond the session: to capture the fix as a standing instruction or a Skill is what stops six schedulers re-deriving it every week. An unrecorded fix is re-derived on every future occurrence, which is decay by another name.

distractors.A: A chat post preserves the text and not the default; every scheduler still has to remember it exists and go and find it.
distractors.B: Tacit know-how is what the franchise has now, and it is why the same problem returns every week.
distractors.C: A rebuild spends a day of reconstruction on a change that belongs in one line of the configuration.

questions.question: A communications officer at a port authority has moved the drafting of berth-closure notices into a configured Project, and the director wants to report the efficiency gain to the board. Nobody recorded how the old process performed. Which TWO steps make the claimed gain checkable? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Reconstruct a before measure of the old process — time per notice and rework rounds
options.B: Ask the communications team whether the new workflow feels faster, and report that
options.C: Move to a faster model tier at the same time, so the reported gain is as large as possible
options.D: Have Claude estimate the time saved across the notices it has drafted so far
options.E: Measure the same two figures after the change, with the workflow instrumented at that level

rationale.correct: Optimization is deliberate and measured: instrument the workflow, find the friction, promote the fix into configuration, and measure the gain. A before measure of time per notice and rework rounds, and the same two figures after, give the board a number it can check; optimizing without a baseline produces an unfalsifiable claim of improvement.

distractors.B: A sense that the workflow feels faster is the impression the measurement was there to test.
distractors.C: A second change made at the same time inflates the number and destroys the attribution behind it.
distractors.D: The model holds no record of how long the old process took, so its estimate is fluent arithmetic over nothing.
